walkthroughs.body_html:
Understanding Business Activity — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Understanding Business Activity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Understanding Business Activity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the 'S' in SMART objectives stand for?
options: Strategic
Specific
Strong
Saleable

mcqs.q: Which 1970 essay argued the 'social responsibility of business is to increase profits'?
options: Drucker
Porter
Friedman
Carroll

mcqs.q: Does adding value mean the same as making profit?
options: No — added value is the difference between the selling price and the cost of bought-in materials; profit only emerges after all other costs are also paid.
Adding value means putting prices up illegally.
Partnerships are only allowed for law firms.
Added value and profit are identical.

mcqs.q: Is a partnership always better than being a sole trader?
options: Having more owners automatically makes a business stronger.
Objectives must be renewed annually with the tax office.
Partnerships are only allowed for law firms.
Not always — partnerships add capital, skills and shared workload, but profits are shared, disagreements arise and most partners still face unlimited liability.

mcqs.q: Do business objectives stay the same forever?
options: No — a new business may focus on survival, then shift to growth, profit or market share as it matures, and objectives change again in recessions.
Objectives must be renewed annually with the tax office.
A business sets its objectives once and never changes them.
Partnerships are only allowed for law firms.
